title: Pseudo-coherent tensor tests detect relative pseudo-coherence on algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived tensor uses K-flat resolutions and $R\Gamma$ uses K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. A perfect object is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Pseudo-coherent on a space means that etale locally on affine scheme charts the object is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free structure modules; pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ means quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above finite-free $A$-complex [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For a locally finite type morphism $g:Z\to T$ of algebraic spaces, an object $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $T$ if for every integer $m$ and every commutative square $U\to V$, $U\to Z$, $V\to T$ with $U,V$ schemes and the vertical maps etale, $L|_U$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V$. Here on scheme charts use [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]: locally factor $U\to V$ as a closed immersion into finite-dimensional affine space over $V$; its derived pushforward admits locally a strictly perfect approximation inducing cohomology isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection in degree $m$. The affine covers, factorizations and approximations may depend on $m$. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a separated morphism of finite presentation, and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts. Suppose $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every pseudo-coherent $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Flatness, properness and Noetherian hypotheses are not required.

proof.text: Fix $x\in|X|$. Choose $n,Z,z,V,E$ from the algebraic-space derived Chow lemma. Put $P=\mathbf P^n_A$, $T=X\times_A P$, and write $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to P$, $W=c^{-1}(V)$, $b_W:W\to X$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow V$ for its maps. Thus $z\in W$ maps to $x$, $b_W$ is etale, $j$ is a finitely presented closed immersion, and $E$ is pseudo-coherent with the stated graph-kernel restriction. We do not assert that $b_W$ is an open immersion or an isomorphism onto an open of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, second paragraph (choice of derived Chow data)

proof.text: For $d\in\mathbf Z$ put $F_d=E\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lq^*\mathcal O_P(d)$. The twist is locally free of rank one. On the inverse images of its trivializing opens, tensor by its pullback is tensor by the structure module, so $F_d$ is locally isomorphic to $E$. Consequently $F_d$ is pseudo-coherent, directly from the local finite-free characterization. The projective-projection clause of the flat proper direct-image lemma gives the pseudo-coherent object $G_d=Rp_*F_d$ on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, third paragraph, pseudo-coherence of the test object on X by 0CTN

proof.text: The pseudo-coherent $E$ and $F_d$ have quasi-coherent cohomology: on each etale affine chart their finite-free models are pseudo-coherent on the scheme, hence have quasi-coherent cohomology by the scheme lemma; etale/Zariski comparison and the chart definition of quasi-coherence give the assertion on $T$. Thus $Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by pullback and tensor preservation. Set $M=Rq_*(Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)$. Both $T$ and $P$ are qcqs (products of the separated finitely presented $X$ and projective $P$), so the qcqs direct-image theorem gives $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_P)$.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, third paragraph, quasi-coherent domains of the two projection formulas and projective twist test

proof.text: Apply the projection formula first to $q$ and $\mathcal O_P(d)$, then to $p$ with $F_d$ and $K$. Using symmetry/associativity of derived tensor and composition of derived direct images gives isomorphisms in $D(A)$: $$R\Gamma(P,M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_P(d))\simeq R\Gamma(T,Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F_d)\simeq R\Gamma(X,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}G_d).$$ The maps $p,q$ are qcqs; no flatness of $q$ is used. The hypothesis of the item applies to $G_d$ by step 2, and therefore the displayed object is pseudo-coherent over $A$ for every $d$.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, displayed pair of equalities and the following application of the hypothesis

proof.text: Apply the etale/Zariski derived equivalence on $P$. It intertwines derived tensor (on flat tensor representatives) and derived global sections, and the twists are the pullbacks of the same Zariski line modules. The Zariski object corresponding to $M$ therefore satisfies the twist tests for $d=0,\ldots,n$. The projective-space twist criterion makes that object pseudo-coherent. Etale pseudo-coherence descent identifies this with pseudo-coherence of $M$ on the small etale site. Restriction to the open $V$ preserves its local finite-free presentations.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, third paragraph, projective-space criterion (0CSG), then restriction to V

proof.text: The transform-restriction lemma now identifies $M|_V\simeq Rj_*(b_W^*K)$ in $D(\mathcal O_V)$. Here the kernel restriction and etaleness required by that lemma are exactly the properties selected in step 1; $K$ satisfies its quasi-coherence hypothesis. Thus $Rj_*(b_W^*K)$ is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, last displayed formula, with restriction to V (correcting the source display subscript)

proof.text: Transport $b_W^*K$ and $Rj_*(b_W^*K)$ to the Zariski derived categories of the schemes $W,V$. The comparison theorem intertwines the closed-immersion direct image (j is qcqs), and pseudo-coherence descent shows that the Zariski direct image is pseudo-coherent. Since $j:W\hookrightarrow V$ is a closed immersion and $V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat and locally finitely presented (locally its coordinate rings are localizations of polynomial rings), the flat-ambient criterion implies that the scheme object $b_W^*K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $A$.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, last sentence: 09UU on the closed immersion W into V

proof.text: For every $x$ the preceding construction gives an etale scheme neighbourhood $b_W:W\to X$ whose image contains $x$, on which $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $A$. Choose one such neighbourhood for each point; these form a set-indexed jointly surjective etale family. Apply relative pseudo-coherence locality for each integer $m$, taking every target chart to be $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with its identity map. It follows that $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $A$ for every $m$, hence pseudo-coherent relative to $A$ with exactly the definition in the item. If $X$ is empty the same conclusion holds by the empty covering case.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, first paragraph and final local-to-global conclusion
